title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
description: Reuse code with class hierarchies and leverage polymorphic interfaces.

blocks.content:
Imagine you're designing an employee payroll system with `Managers`, `Engineers`, and `Interns`. All employees have a `name`, `id`, and `email`, but their bonus calculations and responsibilities differ.

Rather than duplicating common fields across separate classes, **Inheritance** lets child classes inherit attributes and methods from a parent class.

blocks.question: What does `super().__init__(...)` do in a subclass constructor?
options: Calls the constructor of the parent class to initialize inherited attributes
Permanently deletes the parent class from memory
Prevents the subclass from having custom methods
Converts all subclass methods into class methods
blocks.explanation: `super()` delegates method calls to the parent (superclass), ensuring the parent's initialization logic is executed.

blocks.prompt: Write a function `calculate_payroll(employees)` that receives a list of dictionaries with employee data and calculates total payout. Define a base class `Employee(name, base_salary)` with a `.calculate_pay()` method. Subclass `SalesPerson(Employee, commission)` where `.calculate_pay()` returns `base_salary + commission`. Return the sum of pay for all employees.

tests.description: calculates combined payroll of regular and sales employees
